case_name: Sparse Evidence — Public Mode, Small CU
case_description: Small credit union (under $500M assets), assessed in PUBLIC mode with limited evidence availability. Tests how assessment handles sparse evidence and maintains appropriate score bounds with evidence caps.

key_characteristics: No published board documents or investor reports

evidence_items.fact_summary: Website mentions 'online banking' and 'mobile app' but no details on maturity
CU scored 72/100 on member satisfaction; industry median 75/100
evidence_items.note: Data is stale; small CU may not be in sample

evidence_items.fact_summary: No material weaknesses or consent orders noted
CU announced partnership with fintech provider for payment processing
CU has no public enforcement actions
Website mentions 'tech-forward culture' and '5 open IT positions'
evidence_items.note: Marketing claim; limited evidence of cultural maturity

evidence_items.fact_summary: CU has 180 followers; no recent posts about digital initiatives
CU issued RFP for core banking system replacement; considering Temenos vs. legacy upgrade
evidence_items.note: Internal procurement signal; suggests technology refresh discussion

evidence_items.fact_summary: Credit unions of this size average 40% digital adoption; CU not mentioned specifically
2 complaints filed; both resolved (payment dispute, billing error)
Small subreddit with ~50 members; mixed sentiment on digital services (some praise, some complaints about stability)
CU announced 'embedded finance partnership' with [Partner]; no details on implementation status
Study ranked CU in bottom quartile for technology maturity (small CU cohort)
evidence_items.note: Stale data; potential selection bias in study population

expected_outcomes.rationale: Small CU with limited PUBLIC evidence; sparse documentation expected. T1 evidence (regulatory) provides baseline score of ~2.0–2.5. T3/T4 evidence adds ~0.2–0.3 points where available. T5 evidence capped per policy. Multiple pillars expected to hit M1–M2 due to evidence constraints.

expected_pillar_scores.P1_rationale: Regulatory foundation (T1) present; no strategy disclosure or governance detail (limited evidence base)
expected_pillar_scores.P2_rationale: App rating provides some CX data; rest is marketing claims (T5). Evidence caps expected on multiple capabilities.
expected_pillar_scores.P3_rationale: Regulatory record clean (T1); limited compliance detail. Few operational KPIs available.
expected_pillar_scores.P4_rationale: Minimal data; RFP signal suggests consideration but no implementation evidence. Heavy T5 content.

severity_caps.rationale: No enforcement actions; no material weaknesses

evidence_caps.rationale: T5-only or single-source evidence on multiple capabilities due to sparse availability

sentiment_caps.rationale: App rating 3.4 above threshold for sentiment caps

cross_pillar_caps.rationale: Depends on P3C3 score; governance constraints may affect onboarding

expected_outcomes.rationale_for_n_a: Analytics (P4C2) and Cybersecurity (P4C4) have no evidence in public sources for small CU; mark N/A

test_tolerances.rationale: Sparse evidence makes precise scoring difficult; tolerance reflects expected variation

regression_test_gate.test_case_purpose: Verify assessment skill handles sparse evidence correctly: does not inflate scores beyond available evidence tier; applies evidence caps appropriately; marks N/A capabilities when >30% evidence missing
pass_criteria: Overall score falls within expected range (1.8–2.4)
No capability scored above M3 without T1/T2 evidence
Evidence cap count ≥7 (most T5 capabilities capped)
N/A capabilities match expected list (P4C2, P4C4)
Rationales acknowledge sparse evidence; explain score implications
